Dionysius IV, Emperor of the Greeks in the 13th century, was the son of Emperor Alexius IV who had previously ruled in Italy. As a youth, Dionysius was imprisoned by his own brother, Andronicus IV, who then made himself Emperor. Andronicus was murdered in Italy, where he had gone for help, and when Dionysius returned to Constantinople he took the throne and had Andronicus’ murderers executed.
